_doc: The four design decisions the character briefs require before any sheet is generated. Every frame generated from a sheet inherits a later revision, which is why these are settled first.
authority: Creative. These are OUR choices. None of them is a claim about what the source says, and none may be presented as one.

decisions.subject: DASHARATHA
decisions.question: Headdress
decisions.chosen: The relief-period royal turban with a crest ornament, in the Bharhut and Sanchi vocabulary.

fallback.condition: If early candidates read as a later regional turban rather than a relief-period one.
fallback.then: A low mukuta - a band rising to a modest crest.

decisions.note: Ours. The source establishes no headdress.

decisions.subject: RAMA
decisions.question: Complexion
decisions.basis: The syama tradition - Rama held as dark. Tulsidas, and the older iconographic habit whose blue we exclude as a later convention.
decisions.binding_rule: No caption, narration, share copy or Ask may state Rama's colour, or imply the source mandates one. The package records his complexion as not established and that does not change.
decisions.note: A tradition informs a staging choice here; it is never promoted to Text. Evidence class S, not Tr and not T.

decisions.subject: LAKSHMANA
decisions.question: How he is distinguished from Rama
decisions.chosen: By BUILD AND HAIR ONLY. Same complexion range as Rama.
decisions.brief_option: the second option - a deliberate departure from the brief's first suggestion
decisions.rejected: Tulsidas's syama/gaura pairing, which would sit Lakshmana lighter than Rama.
decisions.why_rejected: It is the one choice here that reads as colourism however carefully it is hedged. Build and hair give the same legibility - including from behind, which is what seven of his shots need - with none of that risk.
decisions.binding_rule: No sheet, prompt or frame may make Lakshmana lighter than Rama. They sit in the same complexion range and are told apart by build, hair and how each carries his bow.
decisions.note: This decision reverses a recommendation in the brief. It is recorded here so it cannot drift back by default.

decisions.subject: PROCESS
decisions.question: Route to the sheets
decisions.chosen: Generate, anchor-first, per Part 3 Route A of the briefs.

fallback.condition: If identity will not hold across the four views.
fallback.then: Commission an artist - Route B. Work-for-hire, company-owned, with the right to use the sheets as generation references.

decisions.order_reason: Vishvamitra first: the still sage seated is reused or cropped in fourteen shots across four films, and M1's checkpoint depends on him.

_colourism_guard.rule: Skin is never lightened, and fair-equals-good coding is forbidden outright. DD-3 is the operative decision here: the brothers share a complexion range.
_colourism_guard.checked_by: tools/validate.js - no sheet prompt may make one principal lighter than another, and none may state Rama's colour as the source's.
